messages:
eli: quick question — I'm opening a TF change to expose an internal service via a VPC Endpoint Service backed by an internal NLB in infra-account. Consumers will live in app-account(s). few quick Qs: 1) should we set `acceptance_required = true` and automate acceptance, or leave false for auto-connect? 2) what's our recommended SG model (restrict on NLB vs require SG on interface endpoint)? 3) ownership: infra-account will create the `aws_vpc_endpoint_service` and NLB; app-account will create `aws_vpc_endpoint` resources. any tips for TF state/iam cross-account references? sharing snippet below of what I'm proposing.

eli: ```hcl
resource "aws_lb" "svc_nlb" {
  name               = "svc-nlb-internal"
  internal           = true
  load_balancer_type = "network"
  subnets            = var.private_subnet_ids
}

resource "aws_vpc_endpoint_service" "svc" {
  network_load_balancer_arns = [aws_lb.svc_nlb.arn]
  acceptance_required        = true
  payer_account_id           = "123456789012" # infra account
}
```

tara: I would keep `acceptance_required = true`. safer — we can have a cross-account role that accepts connections from app-account. Also prefer locking down on the endpoint side: require customers to create endpoint SGs that only allow outbound to svc port. NLB SG should be minimal.

tara: pattern we've used: provider in infra-account exposes a small accepter lambda (or automation) that runs once-per-connection using `aws_vpc_endpoint_connection_accepter` to accept requests from allowed principals. That avoids manual acceptance in Slack.

michael: +1 on acceptance_required. also watch DNS: interface endpoints create private DNS entries that resolve to endpoint ENIs in the consumer VPC. if you expect clients to hit the NLB directly (via service DNS), ensure we publish a private hosted zone association or provide the service DNS explicitly. otherwise apps might try to resolve public name and fail.

ana: small TF notes: tag `aws_vpc_endpoint_service` and NLB. add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["dns_name"] }` on NLB if the provider sometimes forces replacement because of DNS churn. and put `depends_on` where needed so accepter runs after NLB creation.

ana: example accepter resource we use:
```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint_connection_accepter" "accept" {
  vpc_endpoint_service_id = aws_vpc_endpoint_service.svc.id
  vpc_endpoint_id         = var.pending_endpoint_id
  # requires permissions in infra account to accept
}
```

devops-bot: terraform plan (sandbox) for branch/eli/privatelink shows: + aws_lb.svc_nlb, + aws_vpc_endpoint_service.svc, no destructive changes. estimated time to create resources ~ 2m. :white_check_mark:

chris: also add an onboarding doc for app teams: steps to create `aws_vpc_endpoint` in their account, how to tag the request, and what principal to use. include a smoke test: curl the service endpoint from a test pod and verify 200.

chris: one more gotcha — if app-accounts are in different aws org units, make sure `allowed_principals` or org-wide principals are set on the service if you want to automatically allow them.

eli: awesome, thanks. i'll implement `acceptance_required = true`, add the accepter automation (lambda + small role), include route53 private hosted zone instructions, and add TF comments about ownership boundaries. i'll open a PR in ~30m and ping for review.
